name: AKU provides 79 Fellows, Residents and Interns to serve the nation

content.text: This year, certificates were awarded to 42 interns. III addition, 35 residents received certificates for completion of sub-speciality training in 11 clinical disciplines. The Best Intern Award went to Ayesha Shaikh. The two fellowships conferred were in Adult Cardiology and Clinical Neurophysiology and Electro diagnostic Medicine. The latter programme is first of its kind in Pakistan. All AKU postgraduate programmes are approved by the College of Physicians and Surgeons, Pakistan and several by the Royal Colleges of the U.K. The last few years have shown a steady increase in the number of applicants to these programmes (30 per cent just last year), drawn from graduate; of 20 medical colleges in the country, including AKU.

In his welcome address, Dr Robert Maudsley, Dean, Faculty of Health Sciences, AKU, noted that the event was "another milestone in the professional advancement of the graduates," as they continued to gain greater medical expertise.

A core curriculum for residents at AKU emphasises no only clinical skills, but also instruction in ethics, communication skills, medico-legal knowledge and computer literacy. In her address, Dr Fauzia Khan, Acting Associate Dean, PGME, hoped that the graduates would take with them their "education and technical aptitude as well as compassion and empathy for patients."

Since 1991, AKU has graduated 282 young men and women from its postgraduate programmes. 68 per cent of these are working in Pakistan, and many are senior AKU faculty members. Even more heartening is that many others are staff and faculty of reputable teaching restitutions throughout the country.

The PGME programme at AKU is providing the nation 1 with an important reserve of skilled specialists. This success in training, over a relatively short time, confirms that good quality programmes in the private sector can play a significant role in minimizing the brain drain, thereby improving health care delivery in Pakistan.

content.author: volunteer.pa
content.description: Major General (R) Ahsan Ahmed, Minister of Health and Population Welfare, Government of Sindh, was the chief guest at the Graduation Ceremony for fellows, residents and interns of the Aga Khan University's (AKU) Department of Postgraduate Medical Education (PGME) on October 28, 2000. He highlighted that, "The aim of the University is not only to train residents in clinical competence, provide quality curative and preventive medical services to people, but also to provide academic leaders, dedicated teachers and specialists for the country."
